name: Iron Deficiency
description: Iron is essential for chlorophyll synthesis and electron transport. Deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis on young leaves, commonly found on alkaline soils and in crops like rice, beans, and cowpea.
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on young leaves (yellow between green veins)
Severe deficiency causing leaves to turn almost white
Stunted growth and reduced plant vigor
Necrotic spots developing on severely affected leaves
Leaf margins may scorch in advanced stages
causes: High soil pH (alkaline conditions >7.0) reducing iron solubility
Excessive phosphorus or heavy metals competing with iron
Waterlogged conditions reducing iron uptake in some crops
treatments: Foliar spray of iron chelate (Fe-EDTA or Fe-EDDHA) at 0.1-0.2%
Foliar spray of ferrous sulfate (1% solution)
Soil application of iron sulfate where appropriate
Apply iron chelates to alkaline soils (Fe-EDDHA preferred for high pH)
prevention: Maintain soil pH in optimal range (6.0-6.5)
Include iron in foliar nutrient programs
